correctness.rationale: For ℓ=2, any two edges in K_{2,k} share an endpoint or have adjacent endpoints, so the conflict graph is complete. For distinct branches at ℓ≥3, cross-conflicts are exactly (1,1), (1,2), (2,1) and their terminal reversals. At ℓ=3 the left-position neighbor sets are {1,2}, {1,3}, {2,3}; for ℓ≥4 the first- and last-terminal patterns have disjoint position sets. Both cases have maximum degree two and no K_{2,2}. Same-branch conflicts are precisely position differences one or two, since there is no extra edge between vertices of that branch. So a within-branch clique has at most three edges and a cross-branch clique has at most one branch with two edges, all others at most one. The first terminal star plus any one second edge attains k+1. At ℓ=4 a (k+1)-palette forces all second edges to one omitted color and all third edges to another. They must differ, but then the third-edge color appears at the first edge of some branch and conflicts with the third edge of that same branch. The explicit (k+2)-color pattern avoids that obstruction. At ℓ=3 the cyclic shift of the first colors on the last edges avoids the same-branch first/last conflict; the middle uses the spare color. At ℓ=5, the last-edge palette omits 1 (the fourth-edge color) and the first-edge palette omits k+1 (the second-edge color); the choices of c_i separate all same-branch pairs at distances ≤2, including i=1 and i=2. At ℓ≥6 the two copies of k+1 are separated by at least three positions, and the interior period-three sequence can avoid i at both contact positions by choice of phase. Those are the only positions of the interior within distance two of a terminal edge. Thus the prescriptions meet every same- and cross-branch constraint, and the comparison with the clique bound proves the claimed gap.
residual_risks: The recorded finite tests are not used as an exhaustive proof. The theorem does not include unequal branches or the k=2 cycles.

evidence: The minor-free bound is 3Δ for the full edge set. The sparse subcubic planar large-girth bound reported in DeOrsey et al. is 5, not the claimed 4. Chang–Duh's equality results require σ≥Δ+2, whereas σ=k+1=Δ+1 for this family. Their corresponding weakened bounds allow σ+1 even when the extra girth or sparsity hypotheses hold.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest inspected general shape of an equality theorem does not apply; the weaker bounds cannot resolve either exact sharpness or the failure of sharpness only at ℓ=4. The exact hypotheses of the inaccessible 2014 subdivision results are not inferred from bibliographic summaries.

evidence: The strong index equals χ(L(Θ)^2), not χ(Θ^2). For even ℓ≥4, Θ_{k,ℓ} is the full one-subdivision of Θ_{k,ℓ/2}, so its strong index is the latter graph's incidence chromatic number. In particular, ℓ=4 corresponds to incidence coloring of K_{2,k}. arXiv:1505.04908v3 states the subdivision equivalence and discusses the related balanced complete bipartite case.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The incidence reduction is exact for the even-length chromatic index and makes incidence literature a real source of possible individual-case overlap. It is not an enumeration of strong edge-conflict cliques or of the full family. Vertex-square theta coloring and strong-odd coloring of the same subdivision are different parameters.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the joint exact classification of the edge-conflict clique number and chromatic index across all branch counts and common lengths, including sharpness away from the exceptional length. No independent novelty is assigned to the K_{2,k} case, the terminal-star bound, or to the length-four index in isolation: that index is an incidence-coloring parameter of K_{2,k} with plausible classical prior coverage. The inspected planar and minor-free results do not imply the full joint classification, and the closest exact theta catalogue hit concerns vertex-square rather than line-graph-square coloring.
residual_risks: Unlocated incidence-coloring results may cover individual even lengths, including the length-four index. The 2014 subdivision full text was inaccessible and could contain more exact cases than its available bibliographic coverage suggests. This is a bounded joint-theorem judgment, not an earliest-priority certification or a claim of novelty for every constituent case.

value.rationale: The uniform theta family gives a natural test of how two high-degree terminals joined by equal-length paths constrain strong colorings beyond their local clique bound. The exact comparison for all lengths and widths identifies when the clique obstruction is complete, and isolates the length-four obstruction rather than relying on a broad series-parallel upper bound. The explicit constructions give useful sharp palettes, including small difficult lengths as well as the unbounded regime. This value is in the full classification, not the trivial complete-bipartite case or a claim that the length-four incidence index is separately new.
residual_risks: The result does not extend as stated to unequal lengths, strong list edge coloring, or unrestricted series-parallel graphs.
